The passage explains that running time depends on input size (e.g., sorting 6 vs. 6×10^9 items takes much longer), so we express time as a function of input size. When analyzing algorithms we usually seek upper bounds on running time because they provide useful guarantees to users (e.g., "will run in at most 3 seconds")—whereas a lower bound (e.g., "runs at least 3 seconds") gives little practical assurance.
